title: Define crystal structures
action: Set up the initial crystal structures (cubic Th3P4-type, space group I-43d) for Zr3N4 and Hf3N4 using the lattice parameter and atomic positions provided in the literature. Create input files for DFT calculations.

title: DFT structural optimization at zero pressure
action: Perform DFT structural optimization at zero external pressure for each compound to obtain equilibrium lattice constant a0 and volume V0. Use Quantum ESPRESSO with GGA-PBE functional and SSSP pseudopotentials.

title: DFT pressure-series optimizations for equation of state
action: Perform DFT optimizations at a series of hydrostatic pressures (0–30 GPa) for each compound to collect pressure-volume data. This generates P(V) datasets needed for EOS fitting.

title: Birch-Murnaghan equation of state fitting
action: Fit the third-order Birch-Murnaghan equation of state to the P(V) data to extract bulk modulus B0 and pressure derivative B0' for each compound.

title: DFT elastic constant calculation
action: Compute single-crystal elastic constants C11, C12, C44 for each compound using the static finite strain method within DFT. Apply small strains to the optimized structure and obtain the stress tensor.

title: DFT electronic structure and dielectric function (imaginary part)
action: Perform self-consistent field (SCF) and non-self-consistent field (NSCF) calculations to obtain electronic wavefunctions and the density of states. Then compute the imaginary part of the dielectric function ε2(ω) from momentum matrix elements.

title: Kramers-Kronig transformation and static dielectric constant
action: Apply the Kramers-Kronig relation to the computed ε2(ω) to obtain the real part ε1(ω) and extract the static value ε1(0). Also compute the static refractive index n(0).

title: Compile final results
action: Collect all computed quantities (a0, B0, B0', C11, C12, C44, ε1(0), polycrystalline bulk modulus B, shear modulus G, Young's modulus E, Poisson's ratio ν, static refractive index n(0), energy of the strongest ε2 peak, and DOS at the Fermi level) for both Zr3N4 and Hf3N4 and write them into a JSON file.
description: JSON object containing all computed structural, elastic, optical, and electronic properties for each compound.
